description: We are Caronte, an intergenerational team from Colombia bringing together two children, university students, and a professor. We share a passion for science, technology, creativity, and space exploration. Through virtual reality, programming, and 3D modeling, we aim to transform NASA's open data into immersive experiences that inspire learning and discovery. Caronte: Different generations, one universe to explore.
summary:
ARMSTRONG: Beyond the Signal is an educational 3D video game developed by Team CARONTE for the Space Mission Design Game challenge. Players become space mission engineers, designing spacecraft, selecting scientific instruments, managing limited resources, and simulating six missions across the Solar System.

Through an interactive engineering laboratory, robotic assembly, and mission simulations, players discover how decisions involving mass, energy, budget, communications, and orbital conditions influence mission success.

Inspired by NASA’s spacecraft technology resources and mission design methodologies, ARMSTRONG translates engineering concepts into an accessible learning experience. Players learn from both successful and failed missions, refining their designs while recovering fragments of a hidden message.

Our goal is to inspire the next generation of space explorers by connecting science, engineering, curiosity, and interactive learning.

details:
ARMSTRONG: Beyond the Signal

Project Overview

ARMSTRONG: Beyond the Signal is an interactive 3D educational video game developed by Team CARONTE for the Space Mission Design Game challenge. It allows players to experience the engineering process behind space exploration through spacecraft design, robotic assembly, resource management, and mission simulation.

How It Works

Players assume the role of space mission engineers and undertake six scientific missions:

  • Earth observation from low Earth orbit.
  • Space telescope operations at the Sun–Earth L2 region.
  • Lunar exploration.
  • Mars orbital exploration.
  • Exploration of Jupiter and Europa.
  • Solar exploration.

Each mission presents different scientific objectives, environmental conditions, and engineering constraints. Players must select appropriate spacecraft components, scientific instruments, power systems, communication technologies, and launch configurations.

In a futuristic engineering laboratory, robotic arms assemble the spacecraft according to the player's decisions. An engineering interface displays how component selection affects mass, power consumption, budget, communications, and mission feasibility.

Players then experience the consequences of their decisions through mission simulations. Successful missions unlock fragments of a hidden message, encouraging players to complete all six challenges.

Educational Approach and Intended Impact

Space mission engineering involves interconnected decisions that can be difficult to understand through traditional classroom exercises. ARMSTRONG provides an interactive environment where students can experiment with these relationships and learn through trial, observation, and redesign.

Both success and failure become learning opportunities. Players can identify engineering limitations, reconsider their decisions, and explore alternative solutions.

The project aims to encourage interest in STEM education, systems thinking, problem-solving, and space exploration among younger generations.

Creativity and User Experience

ARMSTRONG combines scientific simulation with storytelling, interactive 3D environments, robotic spacecraft assembly, and mission-based progression.

The game connects engineering decisions with visible consequences. Instead of presenting spacecraft design only through tables and calculations, players observe how their selected components become part of a spacecraft and influence its performance during a mission.

The hidden signal connects the six missions through a shared narrative that celebrates knowledge, curiosity, and scientific exploration.

NASA Resources and Engineering Principles

The project draws on NASA's mission design methodologies, CubeSat development guidelines, small spacecraft technology references, and orbital visualization resources.

Engineering relationships are represented through simplified computational models involving mass, energy, communications, orbital conditions, scientific performance, and budget constraints. These models are adapted for educational gameplay rather than professional mission certification.

The team considered component compatibility, scientific relevance, resource limitations, environmental conditions, usability, and accessibility when designing the experience.

Development Tools and Technologies

  • Unity — 3D environment, gameplay, animation, and simulation.
  • C# — engineering calculations, resource management, and game mechanics.
  • Universal Render Pipeline — real-time graphics.
  • Tripo — AI-assisted 3D asset generation.
  • ChatGPT and Codex — programming assistance, conceptual design, and technical documentation.
  • Git and GitHub — collaborative development and version control.
  • WebGL and Unity Play — browser-based distribution.

Future Development

The project provides a foundation for additional scientific missions, cooperative gameplay, immersive virtual reality experiences, and more detailed engineering simulations.

ARMSTRONG seeks to make space mission design accessible through an experience where every decision matters and every mission becomes an opportunity to learn.

The next mission begins with you.
